source.title: Disentangling MLP Neuron Weights in Vocabulary Space
source.authors: Asaf Avrahamy; Yoav Gur-Arieh; Mor Geva

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether SAE-derived features aligned to LLM neuron weights explain neuron behavior, using faithfulness and completeness measures. This is a conceptual test of indirect LLM evidence for dictionary-recoverable features, not a test of toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports outcomes for SAE-derived features and random controls, so those are recorded. ROTATE's own results, including its ablations, reconstruction, and initialization consistency, do not measure the claim versions about SAE features or superposition and are not recorded as rows. Other cited findings are not study results.
record.test_reason: A method paper. ROTATE decomposes MLP neuron weights into vocabulary channels and assumes polysemantic neurons mix several monosemantic directions. The SAE features appear only as baselines, picked by dot-product alignment with a neuron's weight vector and scored on how well they describe that neuron. These numbers measure baseline performance against the authors' method. They do not test whether SAEs recover the model's sparse features (V4), whether those features are complete, stable or canonical units (V5), or any toy-model or capacity claim (V1–V3, V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that ROTATE, a data-free, kurtosis-maximizing rotation method, recovers vocabulary channels that are faithful and causally separable. These channels outperform SAE-based baselines on faithfulness and completeness and yield better neuron descriptions (2–3× win rates). They present channels as a scalable unit of analysis and note that vocabulary-orthogonal components are out of scope. They draw no conclusion about superposition or about SAE features as canonical units.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies kurtosis-optimized, weight-anchored rotations to LLM neuron vectors and compares them with SAE features; it does not use the toy-model superposition method or test its overcomplete-feature setting.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports stronger ROTATE gains in middle-to-late than early layers; SAE faithfulness and completeness scores vary by model and layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Single MLP neuron weight vectors decompose into many vocabulary-aligned channels. Ablating a channel suppresses only its own inputs (input-side ablation ratio near 0 for the top channel, near 1 for others) and its own tokens (−87% to −90% self vs +14% to +24% cross). This is evidence that one neuron encodes several separable directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual LLM MLP neurons are superpositions of multiple causally separable, vocabulary-aligned weight directions recoverable without data.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight-aligned SAE features explain neuron activations less faithfully (0.33–0.49) and less completely (0.36–0.49) than ROTATE channels (0.46–0.71; 0.49–0.60).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-stream SAE features selected by weight alignment are not the best units for describing individual neuron behaviour.

record.problems: The evaluations cover two LMs and selected layers. Completeness and description comparisons use LLM judges, though the paper reports a human-annotator validation. Table 1 gives aggregate scores without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant Table 1 rows were left out. ROTATE method results and its separate ablations, layer sweeps, and stability results were omitted because they do not measure the SAE-feature claims or toy-model superposition versions.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity-dependent transition, no geometry.
No test of capacity or feature importance as the cause of polysemanticity.
No test of non-capacity origins of polysemanticity.
No test of whether features are distributed across neurons, or whether SAEs recover sparse model features. SAEs appear only as baselines for neuron description.
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicality as units of the model's representation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests' and T2 labels are wrong. Table 1 SAE numbers are baselines in a method comparison: SAE features were selected by dot product with the neuron weight (top-15 decoder vectors) and scored on describing that neuron. The seed-stability result (cosine 0.9, Jaccard 0.8) concerns ROTATE channels, not SAE features, so it does not bear on V5. Toy Models of Superposition is cited only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or the geometry of superposition in such networks.
It does not test whether feature importance or limited capacity causes neurons to become polysemantic, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
It does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure or whether polysemanticity alone is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE-derived features selected by alignment to individual neuron weights on two instructed LMs and selected layers; does not establish that model features generally spread across many neurons.
Measures behavioral faithfulness and a completeness proxy for selected SAE-derived features, but does not test whether they are stable across runs or canonical units of the model.
The study extracts vector channels but does not test whether the model's underlying features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relation.reason: The assumed mixture of monosemantic directions motivates ROTATE; the study does not test capacity pressure, distributed feature storage, SAE representation completeness or canonicality, or feature dimensionality.

tranche.reason: ROTATE assumes that polysemantic neuron weights contain separable concept directions and evaluates its decomposition method. The SAE comparisons measure neuron-description performance, not any catalog claim version.

source_check.notes: All sampled numbers and conditions match Table 1. Completeness means matching descriptions to one neuron's activating inputs, not completeness of an SAE dictionary as a model representation.
